GOES-07 Energetic Particle Sensor (EPS), 5-minute averages, 1989-10-01 to 1989-10-31, file g07_eps_5m_19891001_19891031.csv (created 2014-03-19), GOES Space Environment Monitor archive, https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/data/goes-space-environment-monitor/access/avg/1989/10/goes07/csv/g07_eps_5m_19891001_19891031.csv. caveats: HISTORICAL REPLAY - NOT CURRENT CONDITIONS. Real GOES-7 measurements from October 1989, replayed so the SPE shelter case can be demonstrated while the Sun is quiet.

Flux = NCEI column p3_flux_ic, described verbatim in the file header as 'P3 Proton ingegral > 10 MeV corrected.' (source spelling kept), 5-minute averages, units p/(cm^2 s sr) (= pfu). The column is labelled 'corrected'; this NCEI archive file was created 2014-03-19 (originating agency DOC/NOAA/NCEP/NWS/SWPC) and may differ from the values behind NOAA's 1989 list. GOES-7's 'GOES Energetic Particle Sensor' is not the GOES-R series SEISS that produces today's data; NOAA states no cross-normalisation has been attempted across GOES detectors.
Values are the archive's own numbers, unrounded, at native 5-minute cadence (no downsampling); the documented missing value -99999 is null (17 of 4032 points in the window).

Event onset/peak/end are computed here with the SESC rule (first of 3 consecutive points ≥ 10 pfu; end = last point ≥ 10 pfu; missing points skipped). NOAA's published list gives start Oct 19/1305 and max Oct 20/1600 at 40,000 pfu; this file gives onset 1989-10-19T13:10:00Z and peak 42,200 pfu at 1989-10-20T16:00:00Z. Whether NCEI time tags mark the start or the end of each 5-minute average is not stated in the file header.

NOAA's list has a single SESC event for this period (start and maximum only, no end time). In this file the >10 MeV flux stays ≥ 10 pfu without a break from 1989-10-19T13:10:00Z to 1989-10-28T19:30:00Z, so the later re-intensifications (see daily maxima) fall inside that one event, as the SESC definition allows; it then hovers near 10 pfu until the last ≥ 10 pfu sample at 1989-10-29T22:20:00Z.

The LANDFALL plan cites NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C [V1 4031], which uses the sum of the October 1989 events as the reference SPE (< 250 mSv). That requirement text was not re-read by this adapter, and this file is a flux time series, not a dose: no mSv is derived from it.

The >100 MeV series (p7_flux_ic) peaks at 531 pfu at 1989-10-20T15:25:00Z in this file, while a footnote on NOAA's SPE-list page gives 680 pfu as the >100 MeV level of 1989 October (NOAA's figure is 28% above this file's peak). Neither source explains the difference; both numbers are kept and no correction is applied.
